g: Rogar que + present subjunctive
‘Les ruego que vivan’ uses subjunctive vivan after a request. The inserted relative ‘que estoy preso’ describes yo.
e: vivan de una manera digna
Vivir de una manera + adjective means ‘to live in a ... way.’ Digna agrees with feminine manera and takes de before llamamiento.

g: Adjectival continuation of the command
The verse has no finite verb of its own: ‘siempre humildes y amables, pacientes, tolerantes’ describes how the recipients are to vivir from verse 1.
e: unos con otros en amor
Unos con otros is the reciprocal ‘with one another.’ En amor gives the sphere or manner in which their patience operates.

g: Affirmative pronominal command
In ‘Esfuércense,’ the pronoun se attaches to the ustedes imperative esfuercen; the written accent preserves the original stress.
e: mantener la unidad del Espíritu
Mantener is the infinitive complement of esforzarse por. The wording treats unity as something received and to be maintained.

g: Existential hay plus así como
‘Hay un solo cuerpo’ makes an existence statement. Así como then adds a comparison: ‘just as you were also called to one hope.’
e: una sola esperanza
Sola agrees with feminine esperanza and reinforces numerical oneness. The preposition a links llamados to the hope of their calling.

g: Verbless parallel series
‘Un solo Señor, una sola fe, un solo bautismo’ continues the hay construction from verse 4; the repeated adjective agrees with each noun's gender.
e: un solo Señor, una sola fe, un solo bautismo
The three balanced noun phrases use repetition to create a compact confession; Spanish alternates solo and sola for gender agreement.

g: Relative clause with parallel prepositions
‘Que está sobre todos y por medio de todos y en todos’ uses one relative subject with three coordinated location or relation phrases.
e: sobre todos y por medio de todos y en todos
Repeated todos gives the three phrases a deliberate rhythm: over all, through all, and in all.

g: Se-passive with duplicated recipient
‘A cada uno ... se nos ha dado gracia’ fronts the individual recipient while nos includes the speaker; the perfect passive presents the gift as received.
e: en la medida en que Cristo ha repartido los dones
En la medida en que means ‘in accordance with the measure that.’ Here it relates grace to Christ's distribution of gifts.

g: Cuando + preterite narrative
‘Cuando ascendió ... se llevó ... y dio’ places two completed actions at the time of another completed action, all in the preterite.
e: se llevó consigo a los cautivos
Llevarse consigo means ‘to take along with oneself.’ The line is presented as a Scripture quotation and uses personal a before los cautivos.

g: Rhetorical ¿Qué ... sino que ...?
‘¿Qué quiere decir ... sino que ...?’ asks what ascendió can mean except that a descent also occurred; sino que introduces the proposed implication.
e: a las partes bajas, o sea, a la tierra
O sea reformulates the preceding phrase as ‘that is, the earth.’ The commas mark this clarification within the parenthesis.

g: El que as a substantivized relative
‘El que descendió’ means ‘the one who descended.’ The same construction supplies the subject linked by es el mismo que.
e: para llenarlo todo
Para + infinitive gives purpose. Spanish commonly combines attached lo with todo: llenarlo todo means ‘to fill it all’ or ‘to fill everything.’

g: A unos ... a otros distributive pattern
The repeated ‘a unos ... a otros’ divides people into appointed roles. Personal a marks those whom él constituyó.
e: pastores y maestros
Pastores means shepherds or pastors; its pairing with maestros, teachers, closes the list of ministry roles in this verse.

g: Nested purpose phrases
‘A fin de capacitar’ states why the roles were given; ‘para la obra’ and ‘para edificar’ then describe service and its building purpose.
e: la obra de servicio
Obra here means ‘work’ or ‘task,’ not meritorious deeds. De servicio specifies that the work consists of service.

g: Relative que + present subjunctive
‘Una humanidad perfecta que se conforme’ uses subjunctive conforme to describe the intended standard toward which the group will develop.
e: la plena estatura de Cristo
Plena means ‘full’ or ‘complete’ and agrees with estatura. The growth image expresses mature conformity to Christ.

g: Coordinated passive participles
‘Zarandeados ... y llevados’ describes the plural niños as acted upon; por phrases name the forces producing the instability.
e: de aquí para allá
This fixed directional expression means ‘back and forth’ or ‘from here to there,’ reinforcing the image of unstable movement.

g: Al + infinitive and hasta + infinitive
‘Al vivir’ means ‘by living’ or ‘as we live,’ while ‘hasta ser’ marks the endpoint toward which creceremos advances.
e: vivir la verdad con amor
NVI uses vivir la verdad, literally ‘live the truth,’ to express truth practiced rather than merely spoken; con amor gives its manner.

v: builds itself up; is built up
g: Participles attached to todo el cuerpo
‘Sostenido y ajustado’ are masculine singular because they describe todo el cuerpo; the main verbs are crece and se edifica.
e: según la actividad propia de cada miembro
Según means ‘according to.’ Cada takes a singular noun, so cada miembro highlights the proper contribution of each part.

g: Negative ustedes command
‘No vivan más’ uses present subjunctive vivan as a negative imperative. Más means ‘any longer’ in this negative pattern.
e: les insisto en el Señor
Insistir normally takes en before a matter; here en el Señor frames the authority or sphere in which Paul makes the appeal.

g: Tener + participle for a resulting state
‘Tienen oscurecido el entendimiento’ presents the understanding as left darkened; oscurecido agrees with singular entendimiento.
e: alejados de la vida que proviene de Dios
Alejado de means ‘separated from.’ The relative que proviene de identifies God as the source of the life in question.

g: Present perfects followed by no + present
‘Han perdido’ and ‘se han entregado’ give completed developments with present effects; ‘no se sacian de’ describes continuing appetite.
e: toda clase de actos indecentes
Toda clase de means ‘every kind of.’ The plural noun actos takes masculine plural adjective indecentes.

g: Fronted demonstrative predicate
‘No fue esta la enseñanza’ places esta before the noun phrase for contrast. The relative que ustedes recibieron identifies enseñanza.
e: acerca de Cristo
Acerca de is a compound preposition meaning ‘about’ or ‘concerning.’ It specifies the subject matter of the received teaching.

v: you were told; he was spoken of to you
g: Si + indicative with passive se
‘Si de veras se les habló y enseñó’ treats the condition as assumed true. Se forms passive/impersonal verbs and les marks the learners.
e: la verdad que está en él
The relative que está en él modifies verdad and locates the truth in Jesus; él carries an accent because it is a pronoun.

v: to take off; remove from oneself
g: Se les enseñó que debían + infinitive
The impersonal/passive ‘se les enseñó’ introduces reported obligation; imperfect debían governs quitarse and looks back to received instruction.
e: el ropaje de la vieja naturaleza
Ropaje makes the former way of life into clothing to be removed; vieja agrees with feminine naturaleza, not masculine ropaje.

g: Passive infinitive in a continuing list
‘Ser renovados’ continues the infinitive complements of debían from verse 22. Renovados is plural because the understood subject is ustedes.
e: en la actitud de su mente
En marks the sphere in which renewal occurs. Su is singular because Spanish uses each person's mente collectively for plural ustedes.

v: to put on; clothe oneself with
g: Infinitive plus reduced passive
‘Ponerse el ropaje’ completes the take-off/put-on contrast; ‘creada a imagen de Dios’ modifies feminine nueva naturaleza.
e: a imagen de Dios
A imagen de means ‘in the image of.’ It belongs to creada and identifies the model for the new nature.

g: Gerund + third-person exhortation
‘Dejando la mentira’ supplies a preliminary action; ‘hable cada uno’ uses present subjunctive as a formal third-person command.
e: miembros de un mismo cuerpo
Mismo reinforces shared membership in one body and supplies the stated reason, introduced by porque, for truthful speech.

g: Si + indicative, then negative commands
‘Si se enojan’ presents a possible real condition; ‘no pequen’ and ‘no permitan’ use subjunctive forms as ustedes prohibitions.
e: hasta la puesta del sol
Puesta del sol is the standard expression ‘sunset.’ Hasta marks the endpoint beyond which anger must not be allowed to continue.

g: Ni continues a negative imperative
The verse depends grammatically on the previous prohibition: ni adds ‘and do not.’ In ‘ni den cabida,’ den is the ustedes subjunctive command form of dar.
e: den cabida al diablo
Dar cabida a means ‘to make room for’ or ‘give an opportunity to.’ Al contracts a + el before diablo.

g: El que + past habit, then que-command
‘El que robaba’ means ‘the one who used to steal.’ ‘Que no robe’ uses present subjunctive as an indirect third-person command.
e: para tener qué compartir
Para gives purpose. Qué carries an accent because it means ‘something/what to share,’ rather than functioning as a relative conjunction.

g: Imperative followed by que + subjunctive
‘Eviten’ directly commands ustedes; ‘que sus palabras contribuyan y sean’ uses subjunctive to express the desired alternative.
e: sean de bendición para quienes escuchan
Ser de bendición means ‘to be a blessing.’ Quienes is a plural relative pronoun meaning ‘those who’ and serves as the object of para.

g: Con el cual relative phrase
‘Con el cual fueron sellados’ refers to masculine el Espíritu Santo. Fueron sellados is a preterite passive agreeing with plural ustedes.
e: para el día de la redención
Para points toward a destined time, ‘for the day of redemption.’ The definite article presents it as a known future event.

g: Imperative governing a coordinated list
‘Abandonen’ is the ustedes command for every item that follows; repeated y joins the final categories in the list.
e: toda forma de malicia
Toda forma de broadens the list to ‘every form of malice.’ After de, the abstract noun malicia appears without an article.

g: Sean + adjectives and reciprocal imperative
‘Sean bondadosos y compasivos’ commands a state; in perdónense, attached se has reciprocal force, confirmed by mutuamente.
e: así como Dios los perdonó a ustedes
Así como introduces the model for the command, ‘just as.’ Los and a ustedes refer to the same plural object, with doubling for emphasis.
